h1: The Nest Private Beach Resort — a quiet private beach tucked into a small cove on Hat Sai Ree
intro: Picture a small resort hidden in a cove on Hat Sai Ree, right next to Mu Ko Chumphon National Park — you wake up, walk straight from your room down to the sand, and barely share it with anyone · The Nest Private Beach Resort is a boutique resort built new in 2021 that guests describe as a genuine private-beach stay, with an infinity pool that looks out over the sea and the islands offshore · It has 21 rooms and villas from around ฿4,500/night · Real guest reviews score it about 8.5, praising the views, the calm, and staff who look after you well

body.html: The Nest Private Beach Resort is a small resort set in a cove on Hat Sai Ree, right next to Mu Ko Chumphon National Park · What sets it apart from the usual beachfront stays in Chumphon is that it really is a private beach — a small cove that outsiders barely reach, and many reviews say it feels like having the whole stretch of sea to yourself · The resort was built new in 2021 and has just 21 rooms and villas, so the mood stays quiet and private — a good fit for couples and anyone who wants to escape the bustle and listen to the waves.

Rooms come in several styles, from a Deluxe with a sea-view balcony (30 sqm) up to a Beachfront Villa (45 sqm) where you step off the terrace straight onto the sand · The top room, the Bird View Villa, comes with a private jacuzzi looking out to sea · What guests praise most often is that rooms are spacious, clean and freshly fitted out — cleanliness scores sit around 8.5 · Several reviewers mention being unexpectedly upgraded to a sea-view villa, which made the trip all the better.
"You walk straight from the room down to the beach — white sand, clear water, almost no one else. It's so peaceful you don't want to leave."

The heart of the place is the infinity pool whose edge runs into the line of the sea, looking out to the offshore islands — it's the spot guests talk about and photograph the most · There's a private beach for swimming or kayaking, a spa and massage room to unwind, and a beachside restaurant and bar called "Rak-Talay" serving both Thai and European food · Many reviews say the food is good and fairly priced, especially breakfast eaten looking out over the water.

Service is another strong point (scores sit around 8.6 in reviews) · Staff are smiling and attentive, and many guests say it feels as warm as staying at a friend's place · The team can arrange a range of activities — snorkelling, island trips into the Mu Ko Chumphon park, fishing, and temple or village tours nearby · It's an ideal base if you want to head out to the islands the next day.

To be straight with you, going by real reviews, The Nest has the trade-offs of a small resort in a cove far from town · The thing mentioned most is that parking is fairly limited and awkward to get in and out of in places · Food and drink options outside the main meals are still thin — sometimes just water and a few snacks · And the peace and quiet comes at the cost of distance: the resort is well outside Chumphon town, so you'll need to drive to find food or shops · Some staff members' English can also be a little limited.

In short, if you're after a beach stay in Chumphon that gives you a private beach, an infinity pool with sea views and genuine quiet, without paying luxury-resort prices, The Nest is a strong pick · A score around 8.5 from real reviews, and a #5-of-26 ranking among Chumphon hotels on TripAdvisor, captures it well — it stands out for its views and atmosphere · It suits couples, honeymooners and small families who want a slow, restful break more than people who plan to head into town every day.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you can, book a Beachfront Villa that opens straight onto the sand — it's better value than a Deluxe set further back · Bring some snacks and water in the car, since shops outside the resort are a fair way off · And if you want to go island-hopping or diving, tell the resort ahead so they can arrange the boat and the trip for you — far easier than sorting it yourself.

honestChecks: If you want to be in Chumphon town often, or wander out for food at night — this place is in a cove far from town, and shops outside are a fair way off → rent a car, or pick a town stay if convenience matters most
If you're driving yourself and worry about parking — parking is fairly limited and awkward to get in and out of in places → arrive in the early afternoon or let the resort know ahead

If you expect the full facilities of a big resort — this is a small 21-room boutique, and food and shop options are thin → bring some snacks, and lean into what it does best: a private beach and quiet

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Nest Private Beach Resort Chumphon

faq.q: Where is The Nest Private Beach Resort in Chumphon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 100 Moo 7, Hat Sai Ri sub-district, in a cove next to Mu Ko Chumphon National Park · It's about 8 minutes by car from the main Hat Sai Ree beach and around 4 minutes from the Krom Luang Chumphon Monument · Chumphon town is about 25 minutes away and the railway station around 30 minutes · The draw is that it's a private beach in a quiet cove that outsiders barely reach.

faq.q: How much does The Nest Private Beach Resort cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿4,500/night for a Deluxe Room with a sea view (30 sqm) · A Villa Deluxe runs about ฿5,200, a Beachfront Villa that opens onto the sand around ฿6,500, and the Bird View Villa with a private jacuzzi around ฿8,500 · Prices vary by date and package, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before you book.

faq.q: Who is The Nest Private Beach Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, honeymooners and small families who want a slow, restful seaside break · The mood is calm and quiet, with a private beach and an infinity pool with sea views · It suits people who want a base for island trips or diving more than those who plan to head into town every day.

faq.q: Is parking and getting there convenient at The Nest?
faq.a: The resort is in a cove about 25 minutes from town, so it's best to drive yourself or rent a car · Worth knowing: parking is fairly limited and awkward to get in and out of in places, as several reviews note · Arriving in the early afternoon makes finding a spot and checking in easier than turning up late.

faq.q: What activities and dining does The Nest offer?
faq.a: There's a beachside restaurant and bar called Rak-Talay serving Thai and European food, with breakfast included · There's a spa and massage room, and a full range of sea activities — snorkelling, island trips into the Mu Ko Chumphon park, kayaking and fishing · The catch is that food and drink options outside the main meals are still thin, so it's worth bringing snacks.

faq.q: How does The Nest Private Beach Resort score in reviews?
faq.a: Real guest reviews score it around 8.5, and it ranks #5 of 26 hotels in Chumphon on TripAdvisor · Guests praise the sea views, the private beach, the cleanliness of the freshly built rooms, and the attentive staff · The main gripes are limited parking, thin food options and the distance from town.
